title: What If You Climbed Everest Without Bottled Oxygen?

scenes.text: What if you climbed Everest without bottled oxygen? You'd breathe the same air, and that's the trap.
At the summit the air is still about twenty-one percent oxygen, but there's effectively a third as much atmosphere.
Above eight thousand meters, the so-called death zone, a long stay without breathing gear leads to decline and death.
In 1978, Reinhold Messner and Peter Habeler were first to do it. Doctors had predicted brain damage or death.
Habeler hallucinated on the last day. By 2016, over four thousand had summited, and fewer than two hundred skipped the bottled oxygen.
The mountain doesn't run out of oxygen. It runs out of pressure.
